claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr has severe lattice distortion caused by the large atomic-size mismatch among Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr.
The lattice distortion forces dislocation cores to adopt wavy, non-planar paths.
The relevant dislocations are predominantly <111>{110} edge dislocations.
The yield strength of HfNbTaTiZr decreases as temperature rises from room temperature to about 900°C.
The elastic anisotropy of HfNbTaTiZr gradually increases with temperature up to about 900°C.
Lattice distortion introduces non-linear thermal expansion relative to conventional BCC alloys.
The test material can be prepared as a homogenized, single-phase BCC HfNbTaTiZr alloy by high-purity arc melting and subsequent thermal treatment.
The BCC phase remains stable in HfNbTaTiZr from room temperature through 900°C under the proposed tests.
A random distribution of differently sized atoms produces modified local bonding environments.
Lattice distortion causes dislocation cores to deviate from ideal planar configurations.
The distorted dislocation cores lower dislocation mobility at elevated temperatures.
Reduced dislocation mobility accounts for a relatively gradual reduction in yield strength with temperature.
Lattice distortion accounts for a modest increase in elastic anisotropy with temperature.
Non-uniform local bonding environments cause non-linear thermal expansion.
The temperature-induced changes in HfNbTaTiZr are smaller than those in conventional BCC alloys.
The proposed behavior is limited to single-phase homogenized BCC samples tested between room temperature and 900°C at approximately 1×10^-4 s^-1.
Phase transformations or very high strain rates may produce behavior different from the predictions.
